summary: Pema Wangdi is a linguist and Tibetologist who earned a PhD at James Cook University (2017–2021). He served at the UN (2011–2013), the Dzongkha Development Commission (2014–2016), and became an Adjunct Research Fellow at Central Queensland University in 2023.
Peng Zhou works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a Bachelor of Philosophy from Hunan Normal University (2013–2017) and a Master of Philosophy from Shaanxi Normal University (2017–2020).

Penghao Sun specializes in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He completed doctoral studies under Leonard van der Kuijp, and studied under teachers including Mark Elliott, Charles Hallisey, Peter K. Bol, Jay Jasanoff, James Robson, Ryuichi Abe, and Qingying Chen.
Penor 02 studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang. He both studied under and taught Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Penor Rinpoche (1933–2009) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure. Educated at Palyul Monastery under teachers including Thubten Chökyi Dawa and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, he founded the Ngagyur Nyingma Institute in 1978 and taught numerous students.

Pent Nurmekund (1906–1996) was an Estonian linguist and Indologist. He earned his Mag.fil. at the University of Tartu (1930–1935) and studied in Copenhagen, Gothenburg, and Paris before teaching and conducting research at Tartu (1955–1986).

Pentti Aalto (1917–1998) worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Helsinki (M.A. ~1934–1939) and Uppsala University, and served as Docent at the University of Helsinki from 1949 to 1980.

Per Kjeld Sørensen (b. 1950) is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar educated at the University of Copenhagen under Erik Haarh. He served as a lecturer at Copenhagen (1982–1989) and as Professor at the University of Leipzig (1994–2017).

Per Kværne (b. 1945) is a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned his Mag. art. and Dr. phil. at the University of Oslo, and held posts at the University of Bergen (1970–1975) and Oslo (1975–2007).
Per Persson (1857–1929) was a Swedish linguist who studied at Uppsala University beginning in 1875. He was appointed Professor of Latin Language and Literature at Uppsala University in 1895.

Per Vilhelm Hilding Juliusson (1916–1977) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He earned degrees from Stockholm University (M.A. 1937–1941; Ph.D. ~1970–1974 under Åke Hultkrantz) and an M.Theol. from Uppsala University (~1938–1944).

Percy Brown (1872–1955) was an Indologist and art historian trained at the Royal College of Art. He served as Principal of the National College of Arts (1899–1909), Principal of the Government College of Art and Craft (1909–1927), and Secretary of Victoria Memorial (1927–1947).

Peri Bhaskararao (1947–2021) was a linguist and Indologist. He was Professor of Phonetics and Phonology at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1974–1999) and held a post at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1999–2007).
Peri Sarveswara Sharma (1926–2000) was an Indologist and linguist. He completed his doctoral studies under Wilhelm Rau (~1968–1971) and held an academic post at the University of Marburg.

Pero Slijepčević (1888–1964) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Geneva and earned a Ph.D. at the University of Fribourg (~1917–1920). He served as Professor of Germanistics at Belgrade (~1928–1941) and Sarajevo (~1950–1964).

Perry Link (b. 1944) is a sinologist who completed his B.A. at Harvard (~1962–1966). He held posts at Princeton University (1973–1977), UCLA (1977–1988), and the University of California, Riverside (beginning ~2008).

Perry Schmidt-Leukel (b. 1954) is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who completed his studies and Habilitation at the University of Munich. He held professorships at the University of Glasgow (2000–2009) and the University of Münster (2009–2023).
Pertti Valtonen (1933–1999) was an Indologist. He earned his M.A. from the University of Helsinki by 1964 and studied under Pentti Aalto until 1968.
Petar Budmani (1835–1914) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at the University of Vienna beginning in 1853 and served as a professor at Dubrovnik Gymnasium from 1868 to 1882.

Peter Adamson (b. 1972) is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at Williams College (~1990–1994) and the University of Notre Dame (~1994–2000). He held posts at King's College London (~2000–2012) and the University of Munich (~2012).
